sentence: This project combines psychometric and machine learning methods to make youth suicide risk prediction easier to interpret and to work across different population subgroups.
This project maintains a breeding colony of pigtailed macaques kept free of specified pathogens, including B virus, for HIV and AIDS research.
This project studies how a transcription factor and a chromatin remodeling complex control activity-dependent genetic programs in neurons, and how a disease model disrupts them.
This project builds a self-supervised deep learning framework for predicting anti-CRISPR proteins and ion and small ligand binding, and for analyzing single-cell data.
This project tests placental tissue and newborn dried blood spots from medical records for genetic risk, inflammation and epigenetic changes linked to autism.
This project studies how membrane lipid flip-flop works at molecular and cellular levels, which is poorly understood.
This project tests whether increasing lysosomal activity in neuronal cells can reduce tau protein aggregation in Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how store-operated calcium channels work and what they do in neurons and astrocytes, including in inflammation-induced depression and neuropathic pain.
This project develops a method using a universal internal standard to measure the protein content of exosomes from patient serum during chemotherapy and radiation therapy.
This project studies how dendritic cells present self-antigens to activate regulatory T cells, and how this helps prevent autoimmunity.
This project tries to treat mucormycosis, a deadly invasive fungal infection, by targeting the host hypoxia-response pathway.
This project develops a prime editing approach for a gene behind blinding retinal disorders, using retinal organoid disease models and preclinical vectors.
This project studies how stress changes alcohol consumption, motivation and neural circuit function, and tests a possible treatment for these effects.
This project uses deep mutational scanning to study the key cell types in checkpoint blockade, a cancer immunotherapy.
This project develops explainable artificial intelligence methods to find biomarkers of aging in multi-omic datasets and to build biological aging clocks.
This project uses long-read sequencing to find genetic causes of recurrent pregnancy loss when current testing finds no reason.
This project uses whole genome sequencing to study the genetic basis of plasma lipids and the risk of coronary heart disease.
This project tests a carbon coating technology for building sub-second neurotransmitter sensors for use in humans.
This project studies the genomic and epigenomic changes caused by prenatal e-cigarette exposure that lead to abnormal brain development in rat offspring.
This project studies how a transcription factor drives a SUMOylation program in neuroblastoma and how a SUMOylation inhibitor causes cell death.
